note: Still the world's largest market (Northern Virginia ~13% of global capacity, 0.5% colocation vacancy and a majority of 2026 capacity already committed, per CBRE H2 2025) with substantial power connection constraints: Dominion has quoted 7-year waits for 100 MW since 2024, had ~54 GW under contract by July 2026 and ~70 GW of requests in queue. The 2026 budget left the sales tax exemption in place through 2035 but added a $0.011/kWh electricity consumption tax from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2028, with revenue above $600M a year refunded. HB 153 requires a site assessment before local rezoning or special-use approval for 100 MW+ projects, and DEQ must define Cooling Water Scarcity Areas by July 2027. The price shown is the unadjusted 2024 EIA average and does not include the new consumption tax.

rr.n: HB 1393 prevents residential cost-shifting for projects of 25 MW or more, HB 496 requires water withdrawal and consumptive use reporting to DEQ, SB 553 makes localities address water supply impacts in rezonings, and HB 153 requires a site assessment before local rezoning or special-use approval for projects of 100 MW or more, with a 500-foot residential setback. The sales tax exemption runs through 2035, but a $0.011/kWh consumption tax applies from July 2026 to July 2028 and DEQ must define Cooling Water Scarcity Areas by July 2027.

rr.n: The 2023 sales tax exemption remains in force. The PSC's May 21, 2026 final decision on We Energies' large-load tariff makes it mandatory above 100 MW, sets a 15-year minimum term and removes the option that let customers pay 75% of generation costs. Local siting disputes are frequent.

Cheyenne rejected a local moratorium in May 2026.
